cards.headline: Black is not dead: it can force a direct ko. White takes it first and neither side has a local threat, so KO−, not DEAD.

diagrams.caption: The tree's line. Black 3 is a wrong answer; the tree marks the leaf S[DEAD], and the solver said KO−.

From the leaf. Black 5 ataris the stone at A17, and White 6 must connect. Black 7 ataris four stones, White 8 fills an outside liberty, and Black 9 captures. White 10 throws in, Black 11 ataris it, and White 12 captures Black 9: a direct ko, taken by White.
As in Diagram 2 up to White 12. With one threat more than White, Black 13 retakes; White 14 has no threat left, and Black 15 captures White 10: two eyes, at A18 and B19.
As in Diagram 2 up to White 12. Without a threat, Black 13 plays elsewhere and White 14 connects the ko. Black 15 captures three stones, but White 16 on the vital point of the bent three kills.

text: S[DEAD] is wrong. Black 5 is Black's only move; the others die. Then White has no better line than Diagram 2: any other White 6 lets Black capture and live, White 8 must fill one of Black's two outside liberties or Black lives outright, and White 10 is the only move that keeps the ko. Black 11 is forced as well: B19 or A17 instead dies.

Black lives if it wins the ko (Diagram 3) and dies if it loses (Diagram 4). White 12 took the ko first, and neither side has a local threat; White 8 fills at F19 rather than A14, which would give Black one. So Black needs one threat more than White: KO−. The solver's ko table and both reviewers agree. The solver's wider-area search left equal threats undecided, but a reviewer found that the extra outside liberties on the real board do not help Black: extending to gain them costs a move.

Changing White 4 does not fix the tree: after Black 3 no White move kills outright, and White's best answers all give a ko. KO− still ranks below the main line's S[ADKO], so Black 3 stays a wrong move.
